correctness.rationale: The full frozen RESULT.md proof expands Walsh quadratic forms in nonzero XOR-character coefficients c_s=2 sum of matrix entries in each matching. Parseval and exact without-replacement finite population sampling give Var(H_k)=(n-k)/(k(n-1)) sum c_s^2; Rademacher quadratic forms give (4/k)sum_{i<j}Aij^2. Cauchy-Schwarz on n/2 edges per XOR matching proves ratio <= n(n-k)/(2(n-1)), with equality iff coefficients are constant on each matching. A=I+epsilon P_s, 0<epsilon<1, gives SPD equality with condition number tending to one. Shared random diagonal signs give expected c_s^2=4 sum_matching Aij^2, hence exact (n-k)/(n-1) factor. Independently evaluated the n=8,k=3 subset distribution to obtain 20/7 sharp ratio and n=8,k=7 boundary 4/7. Matrix must be non-diagonal for ratio; n=2,k=1 equality, k=n Hadamard variance zero. Finite experiments corroborate, not prove, general n.
